about: Abbia Nòva is the small estate of cousins Daniele and Pierluca Proietti, who come from farming families in Piglio, a hill town in the province of Frosinone about 40 kilometres southeast of Rome. Vines have grown on these slopes since Roman times; local tradition says the emperors Nerva and Trajan kept summer retreats here. The cousins work about seven hectares, much of it inherited, alongside olive groves, vegetables and herbs, and they are reviving old local grapes such as Passerina, Bellone and Ottonese next to the area’s famous red, Cesanese.

San Giovanni is one of the estate’s named vineyard plots, and this white comes from Passerina grown there. The farming is organic with biodynamic and homeopathic practices, and the cousins avoid copper and sulphur sprays where they can. In the cellar fermentations start on their own with native yeasts, the wines are neither fined nor filtered, and sulphur additions are kept very low. The appellation on the label, IGT Frusinate, is the regional designation for wines of the Frosinone province.

Passerina is an old white grape of central Italy, long grown on both sides of the Apennines and valued for its lively natural acidity, which suits the cousins’ light-handed, low-sulphur winemaking. Expect white peach, pear and citrus blossom layered with wild herbs and crushed stone. Walter Speller of JancisRobinson.com, tasting an earlier vintage of San Giovanni, opened his note with an exotic nose hinting at apple cider.
facts: Organic, with biodynamic and homeopathic practices
Native-yeast fermentation; unfined, unfiltered; low sulphur
